tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Additional Commissioner (Audit) subsequent to audit of the books of accounts and returns of the company had proposed a demand on the turnover difference due to profit centre mismatch in the trial balance, books of accounts and GSTR9 as reflected in GSTR-9C by issuing SCN dated.30.01.2024 with direction to file reply before the Addl/Joint Commissioner, Haldia Commissioner. The Company filed a reply and subsequently a personal hearing was held before the Joint Commisisoner, Haldia Commissioner. The Company has now received an order from the Joint Commissioner confirming the demand and is in the process of filing an appeal on the order. We do not anticipate any impact on the financials, operations and other activities of the Company.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Joint Commissioner, Haldia, CGST & CX Commissionerate, Kolkata
tax_litigation.status: An Appeal before the Commissioner (Appeals), Kolkata-I was filed on 16.12.2025 against the order received from the Joint Commissioner confirming the demand.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Department had audited the books of accounts of the Company for the period 2019-20 and 2020-21 and compared the GSTR2A ITC as available with that of Table 8A of GSTR9 filed for the period and on the differencial amount arising, concluded that Company has availed ITC on those invoices, where the Vendors may not have filed GSTR3B within prescribed timelines. Accordingly, a demand order has been raised on violation of provisions of Section 16(2)(c) of CGST Act, 2017. The Company intends to file an appeal on the order. We do not anticipate any impact on the financials, operations and other activities of the Company.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Joint Commissioner, CGST & CX, Haldia Commissionerate, Kolkata
tax_litigation.status: A reply was filed against the demand on 4th November, 2025.

operating_notes.text: Nagaur integrated cement unit utilized ₹625.80 Cr of the allocated ₹800.00 Cr IPO proceeds through March 31, 2026.

Received a GST demand-cum-show cause notice of about ₹7.56 Cr (IGST ₹1.22 Cr, CGST ₹3.17 Cr, SGST ₹3.17 Cr) from the Additional Commissioner Central Tax (Audit), Patna, for FY21-FY23 issues; reply being filed.
Existing cement grinding capacity at Nagaur is 2.5 MTPA with another 1 MTPA under implementation.
Q4FY26 total volume sold 3.99 MT (cement 2.35 MT, GGBS 1.57 MT); FY26 total 13.96 MT (cement 7.73 MT, GGBS 5.78 MT).
Operating EBITDA per tonne was ₹916 in Q4FY26 and ₹888 in FY26; adjusted for ₹13.4 Cr FX losses, Q4FY26 EBITDA per tonne was ₹950.
As of March 31, 2026, cement grinding capacity was 24.10 MTPA and clinkerisation capacity 9.74 MTPA; target is 46.00 MTPA grinding and 13.04 MTPA clinker.
Nagaur integrated plant commenced commercial operations on March 30, 2026.
Cement realisation was ₹4,951/t in Q1FY27, up 6% QoQ; GGBS realisation ₹3,807/t, up 3.4% QoQ.
North region utilisation averaged 55% in Q1FY27 and touched 68% in June 2026.
Clinker utilisation was 61% including Nagaur and 87% excluding Nagaur.
Orissa High Court allowed W.P.(C) No. 36871 of 2020, setting aside the 2020 amendment that excluded cement units from SGST reimbursement under IPR 2015.

timeline.summary: JSW Cement received a voluntary ESG rating of 70 (Aspiring) for FY24-25 from NSE Sustainability Ratings & Analytics.
CRISIL released JSW Cement's Q4FY26 monitoring agency report showing ₹1,278.66 Cr of ₹1,600 Cr IPO proceeds utilised, with ₹321.34 Cr remaining in deposits.
JSW Cement disclosed a ₹7.56 Cr GST demand-cum-show cause notice from the Additional Commissioner Central Tax (Audit), Patna, covering FY21-FY23 issues; it is preparing a reply.
JSW Cement adjourned its board meeting for FY26 financial results to May 21, 2026.
JSW Cement announced its Q4FY26 and FY26 financial results and approved a 2.5 MTPA grinding capacity addition at Nagaur for ₹430 Cr.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,894.99 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹371.33 Cr.
JSW Cement Limited shared the audio recording of its Results Conference Call on 21.05.2026 at 5:15 IST via its website.

JSW Cement Limited’s management, led by Sneha Bindra, will attend 360 ONE Capital (B&K) Annual Investor Conference on 29 May 2026 and Citi India Conference 2026 on 5 June 2026, both in Mumbai via physical and virtual modes.
JSW Cement hosted its Q4 and FY26 earnings call reporting 46% YoY jump in operating EBITDA and outlining Nagaur plant expansion plans.
JSW Cement reported Q4 FY26 revenue of ₹1,895 Cr and operating EBITDA of ₹365 Cr, and highlighted the commissioning of the Nagaur integrated unit.
Urmila Kanoria declared no new encumbrances on JSW Cement shares under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) as of April 3, 2026.
JSW Cement held its Q1FY27 earnings call on 14 August 2026, reporting 22% YoY revenue growth to ₹1,896 Cr but a 7.5% decline in operating EBITDA to ₹299 Cr.
On October 16, 2026, the Orissa High Court ruled in favor of JSW Cement, setting aside the retrospective exclusion of cement units from SGST reimbursement under IPR 2015.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,912.15 Cr (+33.1% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹85.35 Cr (-1.2% YoY) (includes ₹20.04 Cr from discontinued operations; continuing operations ₹57.59 Cr).
JSW Cement reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹1,912.15 Cr (+33.1% YoY) and operating EBITDA of ₹277.8 Cr (+3.9% YoY).
JSW Cement Limited hosted a Results Conference Call on 28 October 2026 at 10:30 a.m. IST; audio recording uploaded to its website.
CRISIL Ratings reaffirmed JSW Cement's credit ratings at Crisil AA-/Stable for long-term bank facilities and Crisil A1+ for short-term facilities and debt.
